description: F-CORE-033: a locked account can be unlocked again. `lockAccount` had no counterpart, so a mis-clicked lock could only be repaired by abandoning the account and opening a second one under a new number — which leaves the old one in the chart forever and moves nothing that was posted on it. The question that decided this was whether the irreversibility was LAW: it is not. What the German rules protect against unrecognisable change are postings; for master data they ask that the change be logged, which the audit trail does in both directions — and no other jurisdiction answers it differently either, so nothing about it belongs in a pack. What the lock protects it keeps protecting: while it is locked the account refuses postings, and unlocking changes nothing about the past — every posting ever made on it stays exactly where it is. Both directions are in the trail, as `locked` and `unlocked` with the status diff, which is what makes the sequence readable afterwards.

expect.comment: The lock has teeth while it lasts — that is what it is for.
Posting again is exactly what unlocking permits, and the only thing it permits.
Same refusal as lockAccount: an account that does not exist cannot be unlocked into existence.
The read side says which state the account is in now — before the `accounts` projection existed, the only honest test for a lock was to post into it and read the refusal.
Both directions with their status diff, and the actor as supplied. This is the part the law actually asks for on master data: not that the change be impossible, but that it be traceable.
